solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Digger's mate cut length from clothing

indicators.note: cut ... from means a piece is snipped out of the word for clothing

parts.note: clobber is British slang for clothes

explanation.surface: Someone trims a strip off a garment, as if tailoring for an Australian friend.
explanation.walkthrough: A Digger is an Australian soldier, and cobber is Australian slang for a pal. CLOBBER is British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a cobber is a friend or companion, the kind of comrade a soldier would have.

clue.text: Seven-act plays comprising run for writer

indicators.note: comprising means the jumbled letters hold the run letter within them
plays means the letters of seven-act move about freely

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Seven-act dramas containing a race, attributed to a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' looks like dramas, matching 'Seven-act'; it is the anagram signal. Cervantes, author of Don Quixote, also wrote plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes was the Spanish novelist who wrote Don Quixote.

clue.text: Lad with an eye for the male or female cattle

parts.words: an eye for the male or female
parts.note: someone bisexual, bi for short, has an eye for either sex
a son is a boy or lad

explanation.surface: A boy who fancies both sexes, in a herd of cows.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison is a wild ox, a large bovine in the same family as domestic cows.

clue.text: Always those old English seeing the whole world

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
yon is an old word for those, as in yon hills

explanation.surface: Those old English types always see themselves as the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole world, in the idiom 'the whole world knows', means every person.

clue.text: Gradually extract ten from between the teeth of cutting tool?

indicators.note: extract says letters are pulled out of the word for between the teeth
from completes the instruction, naming the word the letters leave

parts.note: something held between the teeth has been bitten
taken as written
of in the sense of authorship, a book of Dickens being a book by him
a bit is the cutting part of a drill

explanation.surface: A dentist-like instruction to pull ten from between the teeth of a cutting tool's blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extract ten from' takes TEN out of BITTEN, leaving BIT; 'of' is BY as in a work by an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something piece by piece, a little at a time, is doing it gradually.

clue.text: I shall start off cleansing leg with florid rash

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall

indicators.note: start off means just the first letter of cleansing is used

parts.note: in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side
florid means red-faced

explanation.surface: Someone plans to begin cleaning a leg covered with an angry red rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint, matching the leg; it is the adjective meaning hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash decision is one made hastily, without enough thought.

clue.text: African republic welcoming good kind

indicators.note: welcoming means the country takes the good letter inside it

parts.note: Benin is a republic in West Africa

explanation.surface: A West African state welcomes a good sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means gentle and well-disposed, a synonym of kindly.

clue.text: Put a water pipe on account for Australian backwater

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the following pieces are placed after the account

parts.note: a bill is an account to be paid
a bong is a water pipe for smoking

explanation.surface: An instruction to charge a hookah to someone's tab.
explanation.definitionFit: A billabong is an Australian term for a stagnant pool or cut-off branch of a river.

clue.text: Tool to pick up name on inside of clothing

indicators.note: on inside of means the name letter is placed within the clothing word

parts.note: togs is informal for clothes

explanation.surface: A device for picking up name tags sewn inside garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongs are a gripping implement with two arms, used for lifting things like coal or salad.

clue.text: Consider muscle in relaxed state

indicators.note: in means the muscle sits inside the word for a relaxed state

parts.note: rest is a state of relaxation
pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: A fitness instruction: think about your muscle while it is relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect someone is to hold them in regard or take them into consideration.

clue.text: Army to maintain forward movement — about half of them form a union

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is the British reserve army

indicators.note: about means the maintain word goes around half of them

parts.note: to keep is to maintain

indicators.note: half of means only the first two of the four letters of them are taken

parts.note: a lunge is a sudden forward thrust

explanation.surface: Soldiers keep advancing, with about half of them joining forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form a union' looks political after Army; it means marry. TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the plunge is an idiom for committing boldly, especially to getting married.

clue.text: Nothing covering animal's coat? The reverse of that

definitions.text: Nothing covering animal's coat? The reverse of that

indicators.note: the reverse of that tells us to turn the whole preceding phrase back to front

parts.note: nil means nothing
covering means on, as in a lid on a pot

indicators.note: the coat of a word is its outside letters, here from animal

explanation.surface: A puzzle about bare fur: nothing covers an animal's coat, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: NIL ON AL (the coat of 'animal') reversed gives the answer, and the reversal also flips the meaning: wool grease is something that does cover an animal's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the greasy substance secreted by sheep onto their wool, so it literally coats the fleece.

clue.text: Mayonnaise sent back contains this bug

indicators.note: sent back means the hidden letters are read backwards
contains means the answer is held within the letters of mayonnaise

explanation.surface: A diner returns the mayonnaise because there is an insect in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' looks like a restaurant complaint; it signals the reversal, and 'bug' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate or pester them, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Common or garden species of stork sang discordantly

indicators.note: singing discordantly is singing out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An ordinary stork in someone's garden croaked out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common or garden' looks like an idiom for ordinary; here it is literal, a plant that is common and found in gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotgrass is a widespread weed, a familiar plant found in fields and gardens.

clue.text: Call time in middle of day that's first challenge for humanity?

indicators.note: in middle of means the call and time sit inside the word for a day

parts.note: Tues is short for Tuesday
to ring is to call on the phone

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word that's is taken

explanation.surface: Phoning someone at midday as the first test of being human.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turing test, devised by Alan Turing, asks whether a machine can pass for human, hence the question mark on 'challenge for humanity'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turing test checks whether a computer's conversation can be told apart from a person's, testing machine humanity.

clue.text: Pink stone went as high as Bolivian city but not LA

parts.note: to rise to a level is to go as high as it

indicators.note: but not means the letters named next are removed from the city

parts.note: La Paz is Bolivia's seat of government

explanation.surface: A precious stone climbed to the altitude of La Paz, though not Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: LA looks like Los Angeles, another city; it is just the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose topaz is a pink variety of the gemstone topaz.

clue.text: Lots of money including marks, shillings

indicators.note: including means the shillings word holds the marks letter

parts.note: bob is old British slang for a shilling, the plural also bob
M is the abbreviation for marks, as in examinations

explanation.surface: A large sum of money made up of German marks and old shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, nicknamed a bob; 'cost a bomb' is British for very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a bomb is a great deal of money, as in costing a bomb.

clue.text: Ultimate death of wading bird: died after swallowing ecstasy

indicators.note: after means died comes at the end
swallowing means the bird takes the ecstasy letter inside

parts.note: a bittern is a marsh-dwelling heron
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A marsh bird died after swallowing a drug, an ultimate death.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter end is the very last stage, often of a painful struggle, final ruin.

clue.text: Young children holding each article with a light touch?

indicators.note: holding means the young children word clasps the others inside

parts.note: fry are young fish, by extension small children
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Little ones each hold an object gently.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'light touch' is meant literally, as a soft brush like a plume.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resembling plumage is soft and delicate, giving a gentle brush against the skin.

clue.text: Band of commandos at hospital

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment
H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs and maps

explanation.surface: A group of special forces troops arrives at a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group, matching the commandos; it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of fabric worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: Extremely wide cube is a burden

parts.note: dead means extremely, as in dead certain
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide ball
eight is the cube of two

explanation.surface: A very broad cube makes for a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely wide' looks like a single phrase, or even a call for the end letters of 'wide'; it splits into DEAD and W.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead weight is a heavy, inert load or an oppressive responsibility, hence a burden.

clue.text: Journey excluding a grand tour, to put out an excited sightseer?

indicators.note: excluding means the next letters are dropped from the journey word

parts.note: a voyage is a journey
G stands for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: put out means the word to is ejected from tour

explanation.surface: A trip without the grand tour leaves an excited tourist annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put out' looks like annoy; it removes TO from TOUR. 'excited sightseer' is cheeky: a voyeur gets a thrill from looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyeur is a person who gains pleasure from secretly watching others.

clue.text: One's dashed off to pay the rent

definitions.text: One's dashed off to pay the rent

parts.words: One's dashed off to pay the rent
parts.note: a hack work written quickly just to earn money, keeping the pot on the boil; dashed off sounds like someone rushing out

explanation.surface: Someone hurries out of the house to settle with the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed off' reads as running out, but means written hastily: a book churned out purely for income.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a mediocre piece of writing produced quickly for money rather than art.

clue.text: Quiet sound of pain in body cavity

parts.note: P is piano, the musical mark for quiet
ouch is what you cry when hurt

explanation.surface: A soft cry of pain from inside the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouch is a pocket-like sac in the body, as a kangaroo's or a cheek pouch.

clue.text: Link with facilities interspersed in Times2?

indicators.note: interspersed means the letters of facilities are scattered among the letters of the link word

parts.note: to tie is to link
WC, water closet, is a polite name for the toilet facilities

explanation.surface: A link to the Times2 supplement, with facilities scattered through it.
explanation.walkthrough: Times2 is the Times newspaper's features section; read as 'times two' it means doubled. W and C go separately into TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplying by two, two times over, is doing something on a second occasion.

clue.text: Irishman with his head down, counting everything

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letter moves lower, one place down the word

parts.note: Niall is a common Irish name

explanation.surface: An Irishman with his head bowed, totting things up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means altogether or in total, as in 'ten pounds all told'.

clue.text: Many an official who may call out youth

parts.words: an official who may call out
parts.note: an ump, short for umpire, may call a player out in cricket or baseball
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: An umpire may give out a young player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call out' looks like shouting; it is an umpire giving a batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Payment deadline ducked, deducting middle bit

indicators.note: deducting middle means the central letters are taken out of the word ducked

parts.note: bit, past tense of bite, means ate

explanation.surface: Someone dodged a payment deadline by deducting a portion in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like a noun after 'middle'; it is a verb, the past of bite, giving ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A due date is the day by which a bill must be settled, a deadline for payment.

clue.text: Cautiously said tough editor restricts extreme letters

indicators.note: restricts means the tough editor surrounds and hems in the extreme letters

parts.note: hard means tough
A and Z are the letters at either end of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A hard-nosed editor limits the use of extreme letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard a guess is to offer it tentatively, venturing a remark with caution.

clue.text: It's a blinking requirement

parts.note: blinking reads as a mild British swear word but literally you need this flap of skin to blink

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about an annoying necessity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blinking' is a mild British expletive, as in 'a blinking nuisance'; read literally, it is the act of blinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin that closes over the eye is what makes a blink possible.
